===== _commentary/v16/prompts/map3/surah_map.md (adapted) =====
Read the surah as one text and write its map of image chains: the lexical images that run through several of
its ayat and join them into one scene, process or movement. A later writer will read one ayah at a time, with
only that ayah's own dictionary. The map lets that writer hear what the ayah's words carry in the surah as a
whole, including senses whose evidence sits under the words of other ayat.

Your evidence is the surah text, the dictionary of every root in the surah (each branch with the classical
dictionaries' own phrases), an earlier reader's channel review (channels.md),
and your own knowledge of Arabic and the Quran. Where a member or passage comes from memory rather than from
the dictionary or the text, say so. Do not delegate, browse or inspect files; run only the command the header describes.

The channel review is an earlier reader's proposal. Ignore its judgements: grades,
strength or confidence labels, reading types, words such as "surprising", "exploratory" or "latent", and every
statement of what a reading may or may not do. Make your own judgement from the surah's words, the dictionary
phrases and the Quran. Do not rediscover what it already assembled: start from its chains, test each one
against the dictionary phrases and the text, and join, extend, split or correct them. Where its wording
abstracts a member, go back to the dictionary phrase and name what it actually says.

A chain belongs on the map when its members are senses the dictionary attests for words that stand in the surah,
and together they make one image or process that the surah's wording or sequence lets a listener hear. A member
need not be the sense that translates its word in its own ayah; a chain is heard across the surah, not in one
word. A chain may join a sense and its reversal as well as the parts of one scene. Mark a member attested only
inside a fixed expression [fixed expression]; add no other label to a member or a chain, and where a source
records a phrase and rejects it, say so of that phrase alone. When the dictionary itself joins two of the
surah's words in one phrase, quote that phrase: it is the strongest evidence a chain can have. Keep a scene at
the level of its objects, their parts and their operation. When proposals share members, do not fold one into
another's more abstract function unless nothing concrete is lost. Carry every chain that meets this test,
however unusual; leave out proposals that do not.

Write the map in English, with Arabic quoted exactly (surah wording from the text, dictionary phrases from the
dictionary). It is working material for the writer, not commentary prose.

1. `## Chains`. For each chain, a `###` heading naming the image. One paragraph on what the image is and how it
   moves through the surah. Then its members, one line each: the ayah ref, the word as it stands in the text,
   the root and branch id, the dictionary's own phrase quoted exactly, and what this member contributes to the
   image. Add Quran passages outside the surah, with exact refs, where they stage or confirm the chain; for
   each, name the speaker and the situation in a few words, and include the ayah that opens its scene when the
   passage continues one.
2. `## Interactions`. Where chains meet: a shared member, a dictionary phrase that joins members of two chains,
   a Quran passage that stages two chains together, or one chain's scene needing another's. One line each: the
   chains, where they meet, the evidence.
3. `## Ayat`. For each ayah in order: the chains its words take part in, what its words add to each, and in one
   line the whole scene each chain makes across the surah, so that a writer who sees only this ayah sees the
   scene, not a fragment.
4. `## Not carried`. Each channel subchannel you did not carry into a chain: one short line
   each, its name and why, no prose.

No ranking and no labels of strength or confidence. No list of what a writer must include. There is no length
target and no required number of chains or members.

===== _commentary/v16/work/s021/surah.r2/text.md =====
# Surah 21

- 21:1 ٱقْتَرَبَ لِلنَّاسِ حِسَابُهُمْ وَهُمْ فِى غَفْلَةٍۢ مُّعْرِضُونَ
- 21:2 مَا يَأْتِيهِم مِّن ذِكْرٍۢ مِّن رَّبِّهِم مُّحْدَثٍ إِلَّا ٱسْتَمَعُوهُ وَهُمْ يَلْعَبُونَ
- 21:3 لَاهِيَةًۭ قُلُوبُهُمْ ۗ وَأَسَرُّوا۟ ٱلنَّجْوَى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا۟ هَلْ هَٰذَآ إِلَّا بَشَرٌۭ مِّثْلُكُمْ ۖ أَفَتَأْتُونَ ٱلسِّحْرَ وَأَنتُمْ تُبْصِرُونَ
- 21:4 قَالَ رَبِّى يَعْلَمُ ٱلْقَوْلَ فِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ ۖ وَهُوَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلْعَلِيمُ
- 21:5 بَلْ قَالُوٓا۟ أَضْغَٰثُ أَحْلَٰمٍۭ بَلِ ٱفْتَرَىٰهُ بَلْ هُوَ شَاعِرٌۭ فَلْيَأْتِنَا بِـَٔايَةٍۢ كَمَآ أُرْسِلَ ٱلْأَوَّلُونَ
- 21:6 مَآ ءَامَنَتْ قَبْلَهُم مِّن قَرْيَةٍ أَهْلَكْنَٰهَآ ۖ أَفَهُمْ يُؤْمِنُونَ
- 21:7 وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَا قَبْلَكَ إِلَّا رِجَالًۭا نُّوحِىٓ إِلَيْهِمْ ۖ فَسْـَٔلُوٓا۟ أَهْلَ ٱلذِّكْرِ إِن كُنتُمْ لَا تَعْلَمُونَ
- 21:8 وَمَا جَعَلْنَٰهُمْ جَسَدًۭا لَّا يَأْكُلُونَ ٱلطَّعَامَ وَمَا كَانُوا۟ خَٰلِدِينَ
- 21:9 ثُمَّ صَدَقْنَٰهُمُ ٱلْوَعْدَ فَأَنجَيْنَٰهُمْ وَمَن نَّشَآءُ وَأَهْلَكْنَا ٱلْمُسْرِفِينَ
- 21:10 لَقَدْ أَنزَلْنَآ إِلَيْكُمْ كِتَٰبًۭا فِيهِ ذِكْرُكُمْ ۖ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ
- 21:11 وَكَمْ قَصَمْنَا مِن قَرْيَةٍۢ كَانَتْ ظَالِمَةًۭ وَأَنشَأْنَا بَعْدَهَا قَوْمًا ءَاخَرِينَ
- 21:12 فَلَمَّآ أَحَسُّوا۟ بَأْسَنَآ إِذَا هُم مِّنْهَا يَرْكُضُونَ
- 21:13 لَا تَرْكُضُوا۟ وَٱرْجِعُوٓا۟ إِلَىٰ مَآ أُتْرِفْتُمْ فِيهِ وَمَسَٰكِنِكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُسْـَٔلُونَ
- 21:14 قَالُوا۟ يَٰوَيْلَنَآ إِنَّا كُنَّا ظَٰلِمِينَ
- 21:15 فَمَا زَالَت تِّلْكَ دَعْوَىٰهُمْ حَتَّىٰ جَعَلْنَٰهُمْ حَصِيدًا خَٰمِدِينَ
- 21:16 وَمَا خَلَقْنَا ٱلسَّمَآءَ وَٱلْأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا لَٰعِبِينَ
- 21:17 لَوْ أَرَدْنَآ أَن نَّتَّخِذَ لَهْوًۭا لَّٱتَّخَذْنَٰهُ مِن لَّدُنَّآ إِن كُنَّا فَٰعِلِينَ
- 21:18 بَلْ نَقْذِفُ بِٱلْحَقِّ عَلَى ٱلْبَٰطِلِ فَيَدْمَغُهُۥ فَإِذَا هُوَ زَاهِقٌۭ ۚ وَلَكُمُ ٱلْوَيْلُ مِمَّا تَصِفُونَ
- 21:19 وَلَهُۥ مَن فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ ۚ وَمَنْ عِندَهُۥ لَا يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ عَنْ عِبَادَتِهِۦ وَلَا يَسْتَحْسِرُونَ
- 21:20 يُسَبِّحُونَ ٱلَّيْلَ وَٱلنَّهَارَ لَا يَفْتُرُونَ
- 21:21 أَمِ ٱتَّخَذُوٓا۟ ءَالِهَةًۭ مِّنَ ٱلْأَرْضِ هُمْ يُنشِرُونَ
- 21:22 لَوْ كَانَ فِيهِمَآ ءَالِهَةٌ إِلَّا ٱللَّهُ لَفَسَدَتَا ۚ فَسُبْحَٰنَ ٱللَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلْعَرْشِ عَمَّا يَصِفُونَ
- 21:23 لَا يُسْـَٔلُ عَمَّا يَفْعَلُ وَهُمْ يُسْـَٔلُونَ
- 21:24 أَمِ ٱتَّخَذُوا۟ مِن دُونِهِۦٓ ءَالِهَةًۭ ۖ قُلْ هَاتُوا۟ بُرْهَٰنَكُمْ ۖ هَٰذَا ذِكْرُ مَن مَّعِىَ وَذِكْرُ مَن قَبْلِى ۗ بَلْ أَكْثَرُهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ ٱلْحَقَّ ۖ فَهُم مُّعْرِضُونَ
- 21:25 وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن قَبْلِكَ مِن رَّسُولٍ إِلَّا نُوحِىٓ إِلَيْهِ أَنَّهُۥ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّآ أَنَا۠ فَٱعْبُدُونِ
- 21:26 وَقَالُوا۟ ٱتَّخَذَ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنُ وَلَدًۭا ۗ سُبْحَٰنَهُۥ ۚ بَلْ عِبَادٌۭ مُّكْرَمُونَ
- 21:27 لَا يَسْبِقُونَهُۥ بِٱلْقَوْلِ وَهُم بِأَمْرِهِۦ يَعْمَلُونَ
- 21:28 يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ وَلَا يَشْفَعُونَ إِلَّا لِمَنِ ٱرْتَضَىٰ وَهُم مِّنْ خَشْيَتِهِۦ مُشْفِقُونَ
- 21:29 ۞ وَمَن يَقُلْ مِنْهُمْ إِنِّىٓ إِلَٰهٌۭ مِّن دُونِهِۦ فَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِيهِ جَهَنَّمَ ۚ كَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِى ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
- 21:30 أَوَلَمْ يَرَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓا۟ أَنَّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ كَانَتَا رَتْقًۭا فَفَتَقْنَٰهُمَا ۖ وَجَعَلْنَا مِنَ ٱلْمَآءِ كُلَّ شَىْءٍ حَىٍّ ۖ أَفَلَا يُؤْمِنُونَ
- 21:31 وَجَعَلْنَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ رَوَٰسِىَ أَن تَمِيدَ بِهِمْ وَجَعَلْنَا فِيهَا فِجَاجًۭا سُبُلًۭا لَّعَلَّهُمْ يَهْتَدُونَ
- 21:32 وَجَعَلْنَا ٱلسَّمَآءَ سَقْفًۭا مَّحْفُوظًۭا ۖ وَهُمْ عَنْ ءَايَٰتِهَا مُعْرِضُونَ
- 21:33 وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ ٱلَّيْلَ وَٱلنَّهَارَ وَٱلشَّمْسَ وَٱلْقَمَرَ ۖ كُلٌّۭ فِى فَلَكٍۢ يَسْبَحُونَ
- 21:34 وَمَا جَعَلْنَا لِبَشَرٍۢ مِّن قَبْلِكَ ٱلْخُلْدَ ۖ أَفَإِي۟ن مِّتَّ فَهُمُ ٱلْخَٰلِدُونَ
- 21:35 كُلُّ نَفْسٍۢ ذَآئِقَةُ ٱلْمَوْتِ ۗ وَنَبْلُوكُم بِٱلشَّرِّ وَٱلْخَيْرِ فِتْنَةًۭ ۖ وَإِلَيْنَا تُرْجَعُونَ
- 21:36 وَإِذَا رَءَاكَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓا۟ إِن يَتَّخِذُونَكَ إِلَّا هُزُوًا أَهَٰذَا ٱلَّذِى يَذْكُرُ ءَالِهَتَكُمْ وَهُم بِذِكْرِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ هُمْ كَٰفِرُونَ
- 21:37 خُلِقَ ٱلْإِنسَٰنُ مِنْ عَجَلٍۢ ۚ سَأُو۟رِيكُمْ ءَايَٰتِى فَلَا تَسْتَعْجِلُونِ
- 21:38 وَيَقُولُونَ مَتَىٰ هَٰذَا ٱلْوَعْدُ إِن كُنتُمْ صَٰدِقِينَ
- 21:39 لَوْ يَعْلَمُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ حِينَ لَا يَكُفُّونَ عَن وُجُوهِهِمُ ٱلنَّارَ وَلَا عَن ظُهُورِهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يُنصَرُونَ
- 21:40 بَلْ تَأْتِيهِم بَغْتَةًۭ فَتَبْهَتُهُمْ فَلَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ رَدَّهَا وَلَا هُمْ يُنظَرُونَ
- 21:41 وَلَقَدِ ٱسْتُهْزِئَ بِرُسُلٍۢ مِّن قَبْلِكَ فَحَاقَ بِٱلَّذِينَ سَخِرُوا۟ مِنْهُم مَّا كَانُوا۟ بِهِۦ يَسْتَهْزِءُونَ
- 21:42 قُلْ مَن يَكْلَؤُكُم بِٱلَّيْلِ وَٱلنَّهَارِ مِنَ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ۗ بَلْ هُمْ عَن ذِكْرِ رَبِّهِم مُّعْرِضُونَ
- 21:43 أَمْ لَهُمْ ءَالِهَةٌۭ تَمْنَعُهُم مِّن دُونِنَا ۚ لَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ نَصْرَ أَنفُسِهِمْ وَلَا هُم مِّنَّا يُصْحَبُونَ
- 21:44 بَلْ مَتَّعْنَا هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ وَءَابَآءَهُمْ حَتَّىٰ طَالَ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْعُمُرُ ۗ أَفَلَا يَرَوْنَ أَنَّا نَأْتِى ٱلْأَرْضَ نَنقُصُهَا مِنْ أَطْرَافِهَآ ۚ أَفَهُمُ ٱلْغَٰلِبُونَ
- 21:45 قُلْ إِنَّمَآ أُنذِرُكُم بِٱلْوَحْىِ ۚ وَلَا يَسْمَعُ ٱلصُّمُّ ٱلدُّعَآءَ إِذَا مَا يُنذَرُونَ
- 21:46 وَلَئِن مَّسَّتْهُمْ نَفْحَةٌۭ مِّنْ عَذَابِ رَبِّكَ لَيَقُولُنَّ يَٰوَيْلَنَآ إِنَّا كُنَّا ظَٰلِمِينَ
- 21:47 وَنَضَعُ ٱلْمَوَٰزِينَ ٱلْقِسْطَ لِيَوْمِ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ فَلَا تُظْلَمُ نَفْسٌۭ شَيْـًۭٔا ۖ وَإِن كَانَ مِثْقَالَ حَبَّةٍۢ مِّنْ خَرْدَلٍ أَتَيْنَا بِهَا ۗ وَكَفَىٰ بِنَا حَٰسِبِينَ
- 21:48 وَلَقَدْ ءَاتَيْنَا مُوسَىٰ وَهَٰرُونَ ٱلْفُرْقَانَ وَضِيَآءًۭ وَذِكْرًۭا لِّلْمُتَّقِينَ
- 21:49 ٱلَّذِينَ يَخْشَوْنَ رَبَّهُم بِٱلْغَيْبِ وَهُم مِّنَ ٱلسَّاعَةِ مُشْفِقُونَ
- 21:50 وَهَٰذَا ذِكْرٌۭ مُّبَارَكٌ أَنزَلْنَٰهُ ۚ أَفَأَنتُمْ لَهُۥ مُنكِرُونَ
- 21:51 ۞ وَلَقَدْ ءَاتَيْنَآ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ رُشْدَهُۥ مِن قَبْلُ وَكُنَّا بِهِۦ عَٰلِمِينَ
- 21:52 إِذْ قَالَ لِأَبِيهِ وَقَوْمِهِۦ مَا هَٰذِهِ ٱلتَّمَاثِيلُ ٱلَّتِىٓ أَنتُمْ لَهَا عَٰكِفُونَ
- 21:53 قَالُوا۟ وَجَدْنَآ ءَابَآءَنَا لَهَا عَٰبِدِينَ
- 21:54 قَالَ لَقَدْ كُنتُمْ أَنتُمْ وَءَابَآؤُكُمْ فِى ضَلَٰلٍۢ مُّبِينٍۢ
- 21:55 قَالُوٓا۟ أَجِئْتَنَا بِٱلْحَقِّ أَمْ أَنتَ مِنَ ٱللَّٰعِبِينَ
- 21:56 قَالَ بَل رَّبُّكُمْ رَبُّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ ٱلَّذِى فَطَرَهُنَّ وَأَنَا۠ عَلَىٰ ذَٰلِكُم مِّنَ ٱلشَّٰهِدِينَ
- 21:57 وَتَٱللَّهِ لَأَكِيدَنَّ أَصْنَٰمَكُم بَعْدَ أَن تُوَلُّوا۟ مُدْبِرِينَ
- 21:58 فَجَعَلَهُمْ جُذَٰذًا إِلَّا كَبِيرًۭا لَّهُمْ لَعَلَّهُمْ إِلَيْهِ يَرْجِعُونَ
- 21:59 قَالُوا۟ مَن فَعَلَ هَٰذَا بِـَٔالِهَتِنَآ إِنَّهُۥ لَمِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
- 21:60 قَالُوا۟ سَمِعْنَا فَتًۭى يَذْكُرُهُمْ يُقَالُ لَهُۥٓ إِبْرَٰهِيمُ
- 21:61 قَالُوا۟ فَأْتُوا۟ بِهِۦ عَلَىٰٓ أَعْيُنِ ٱلنَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَشْهَدُونَ
- 21:62 قَالُوٓا۟ ءَأَنتَ فَعَلْتَ هَٰذَا بِـَٔالِهَتِنَا يَٰٓإِبْرَٰهِيمُ
- 21:63 قَالَ بَلْ فَعَلَهُۥ كَبِيرُهُمْ هَٰذَا فَسْـَٔلُوهُمْ إِن كَانُوا۟ يَنطِقُونَ
- 21:64 فَرَجَعُوٓا۟ إِلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِهِمْ فَقَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّكُمْ أَنتُمُ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ
- 21:65 ثُمَّ نُكِسُوا۟ عَلَىٰ رُءُوسِهِمْ لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ مَا هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ يَنطِقُونَ
- 21:66 قَالَ أَفَتَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَا يَنفَعُكُمْ شَيْـًۭٔا وَلَا يَضُرُّكُمْ
- 21:67 أُفٍّۢ لَّكُمْ وَلِمَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ ۖ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ
- 21:68 قَالُوا۟ حَرِّقُوهُ وَٱنصُرُوٓا۟ ءَالِهَتَكُمْ إِن كُنتُمْ فَٰعِلِينَ
- 21:69 قُلْنَا يَٰنَارُ كُونِى بَرْدًۭا وَسَلَٰمًا عَلَىٰٓ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ
- 21:70 وَأَرَادُوا۟ بِهِۦ كَيْدًۭا فَجَعَلْنَٰهُمُ ٱلْأَخْسَرِينَ
- 21:71 وَنَجَّيْنَٰهُ وَلُوطًا إِلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ ٱلَّتِى بَٰرَكْنَا فِيهَا لِلْعَٰلَمِينَ
- 21:72 وَوَهَبْنَا لَهُۥٓ إِسْحَٰقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ نَافِلَةًۭ ۖ وَكُلًّۭا جَعَلْنَا صَٰلِحِينَ
- 21:73 وَجَعَلْنَٰهُمْ أَئِمَّةًۭ يَهْدُونَ بِأَمْرِنَا وَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْهِمْ فِعْلَ ٱلْخَيْرَٰتِ وَإِقَامَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةِ وَإِيتَآءَ ٱلزَّكَوٰةِ ۖ وَكَانُوا۟ لَنَا عَٰبِدِينَ
- 21:74 وَلُوطًا ءَاتَيْنَٰهُ حُكْمًۭا وَعِلْمًۭا وَنَجَّيْنَٰهُ مِنَ ٱلْقَرْيَةِ ٱلَّتِى كَانَت تَّعْمَلُ ٱلْخَبَٰٓئِثَ ۗ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ قَوْمَ سَوْءٍۢ فَٰسِقِينَ
- 21:75 وَأَدْخَلْنَٰهُ فِى رَحْمَتِنَآ ۖ إِنَّهُۥ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
- 21:76 وَنُوحًا إِذْ نَادَىٰ مِن قَبْلُ فَٱسْتَجَبْنَا لَهُۥ فَنَجَّيْنَٰهُ وَأَهْلَهُۥ مِنَ ٱلْكَرْبِ ٱلْعَظِيمِ
- 21:77 وَنَصَرْنَٰهُ مِنَ ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا۟ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآ ۚ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ قَوْمَ سَوْءٍۢ فَأَغْرَقْنَٰهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ
- 21:78 وَدَاوُۥدَ وَسُلَيْمَٰنَ إِذْ يَحْكُمَانِ فِى ٱلْحَرْثِ إِذْ نَفَشَتْ فِيهِ غَنَمُ ٱلْقَوْمِ وَكُنَّا لِحُكْمِهِمْ شَٰهِدِينَ
- 21:79 فَفَهَّمْنَٰهَا سُلَيْمَٰنَ ۚ وَكُلًّا ءَاتَيْنَا حُكْمًۭا وَعِلْمًۭا ۚ وَسَخَّرْنَا مَعَ دَاوُۥدَ ٱلْجِبَالَ يُسَبِّحْنَ وَٱلطَّيْرَ ۚ وَكُنَّا فَٰعِلِينَ
- 21:80 وَعَلَّمْنَٰهُ صَنْعَةَ لَبُوسٍۢ لَّكُمْ لِتُحْصِنَكُم مِّنۢ بَأْسِكُمْ ۖ فَهَلْ أَنتُمْ شَٰكِرُونَ
- 21:81 وَلِسُلَيْمَٰنَ ٱلرِّيحَ عَاصِفَةًۭ تَجْرِى بِأَمْرِهِۦٓ إِلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ ٱلَّتِى بَٰرَكْنَا فِيهَا ۚ وَكُنَّا بِكُلِّ شَىْءٍ عَٰلِمِينَ
- 21:82 وَمِنَ ٱلشَّيَٰطِينِ مَن يَغُوصُونَ لَهُۥ وَيَعْمَلُونَ عَمَلًۭا دُونَ ذَٰلِكَ ۖ وَكُنَّا لَهُمْ حَٰفِظِينَ
- 21:83 ۞ وَأَيُّوبَ إِذْ نَادَىٰ رَبَّهُۥٓ أَنِّى مَسَّنِىَ ٱلضُّرُّ وَأَنتَ أَرْحَمُ ٱلرَّٰحِمِينَ
- 21:84 فَٱسْتَجَبْنَا لَهُۥ فَكَشَفْنَا مَا بِهِۦ مِن ضُرٍّۢ ۖ وَءَاتَيْنَٰهُ أَهْلَهُۥ وَمِثْلَهُم مَّعَهُمْ رَحْمَةًۭ مِّنْ عِندِنَا وَذِكْرَىٰ لِلْعَٰبِدِينَ
- 21:85 وَإِسْمَٰعِيلَ وَإِدْرِيسَ وَذَا ٱلْكِفْلِ ۖ كُلٌّۭ مِّنَ ٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ
- 21:86 وَأَدْخَلْنَٰهُمْ فِى رَحْمَتِنَآ ۖ إِنَّهُم مِّنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
- 21:87 وَذَا ٱلنُّونِ إِذ ذَّهَبَ مُغَٰضِبًۭا فَظَنَّ أَن لَّن نَّقْدِرَ عَلَيْهِ فَنَادَىٰ فِى ٱلظُّلُمَٰتِ أَن لَّآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّآ أَنتَ سُبْحَٰنَكَ إِنِّى كُنتُ مِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
- 21:88 فَٱسْتَجَبْنَا لَهُۥ وَنَجَّيْنَٰهُ مِنَ ٱلْغَمِّ ۚ وَكَذَٰلِكَ نُۨجِى ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
- 21:89 وَزَكَرِيَّآ إِذْ نَادَىٰ رَبَّهُۥ رَبِّ لَا تَذَرْنِى فَرْدًۭا وَأَنتَ خَيْرُ ٱلْوَٰرِثِينَ
- 21:90 فَٱسْتَجَبْنَا لَهُۥ وَوَهَبْنَا لَهُۥ يَحْيَىٰ وَأَصْلَحْنَا لَهُۥ زَوْجَهُۥٓ ۚ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ يُسَٰرِعُونَ فِى ٱلْخَيْرَٰتِ وَيَدْعُونَنَا رَغَبًۭا وَرَهَبًۭا ۖ وَكَانُوا۟ لَنَا خَٰشِعِينَ
- 21:91 وَٱلَّتِىٓ أَحْصَنَتْ فَرْجَهَا فَنَفَخْنَا فِيهَا مِن رُّوحِنَا وَجَعَلْنَٰهَا وَٱبْنَهَآ ءَايَةًۭ لِّلْعَٰلَمِينَ
- 21:92 إِنَّ هَٰذِهِۦٓ أُمَّتُكُمْ أُمَّةًۭ وَٰحِدَةًۭ وَأَنَا۠ رَبُّكُمْ فَٱعْبُدُونِ
- 21:93 وَتَقَطَّعُوٓا۟ أَمْرَهُم بَيْنَهُمْ ۖ كُلٌّ إِلَيْنَا رَٰجِعُونَ
- 21:94 فَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌۭ فَلَا كُفْرَانَ لِسَعْيِهِۦ وَإِنَّا لَهُۥ كَٰتِبُونَ
- 21:95 وَحَرَٰمٌ عَلَىٰ قَرْيَةٍ أَهْلَكْنَٰهَآ أَنَّهُمْ لَا يَرْجِعُونَ
- 21:96 حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا فُتِحَتْ يَأْجُوجُ وَمَأْجُوجُ وَهُم مِّن كُلِّ حَدَبٍۢ يَنسِلُونَ
- 21:97 وَٱقْتَرَبَ ٱلْوَعْدُ ٱلْحَقُّ فَإِذَا هِىَ شَٰخِصَةٌ أَبْصَٰرُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ يَٰوَيْلَنَا قَدْ كُنَّا فِى غَفْلَةٍۢ مِّنْ هَٰذَا بَلْ كُنَّا ظَٰلِمِينَ
- 21:98 إِنَّكُمْ وَمَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ حَصَبُ جَهَنَّمَ أَنتُمْ لَهَا وَٰرِدُونَ
- 21:99 لَوْ كَانَ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ ءَالِهَةًۭ مَّا وَرَدُوهَا ۖ وَكُلٌّۭ فِيهَا خَٰلِدُونَ
- 21:100 لَهُمْ فِيهَا زَفِيرٌۭ وَهُمْ فِيهَا لَا يَسْمَعُونَ
- 21:101 إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ سَبَقَتْ لَهُم مِّنَّا ٱلْحُسْنَىٰٓ أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ عَنْهَا مُبْعَدُونَ
- 21:102 لَا يَسْمَعُونَ حَسِيسَهَا ۖ وَهُمْ فِى مَا ٱشْتَهَتْ أَنفُسُهُمْ خَٰلِدُونَ
- 21:103 لَا يَحْزُنُهُمُ ٱلْفَزَعُ ٱلْأَكْبَرُ وَتَتَلَقَّىٰهُمُ ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ هَٰذَا يَوْمُكُمُ ٱلَّذِى كُنتُمْ تُوعَدُونَ
- 21:104 يَوْمَ نَطْوِى ٱلسَّمَآءَ كَطَىِّ ٱلسِّجِلِّ لِلْكُتُبِ ۚ كَمَا بَدَأْنَآ أَوَّلَ خَلْقٍۢ نُّعِيدُهُۥ ۚ وَعْدًا عَلَيْنَآ ۚ إِنَّا كُنَّا فَٰعِلِينَ
- 21:105 وَلَقَدْ كَتَبْنَا فِى ٱلزَّبُورِ مِنۢ بَعْدِ ٱلذِّكْرِ أَنَّ ٱلْأَرْضَ يَرِثُهَا عِبَادِىَ ٱلصَّٰلِحُونَ
- 21:106 إِنَّ فِى هَٰذَا لَبَلَٰغًۭا لِّقَوْمٍ عَٰبِدِينَ
- 21:107 وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَٰكَ إِلَّا رَحْمَةًۭ لِّلْعَٰلَمِينَ
- 21:108 قُلْ إِنَّمَا يُوحَىٰٓ إِلَىَّ أَنَّمَآ إِلَٰهُكُمْ إِلَٰهٌۭ وَٰحِدٌۭ ۖ فَهَلْ أَنتُم مُّسْلِمُونَ
- 21:109 فَإِن تَوَلَّوْا۟ فَقُلْ ءَاذَنتُكُمْ عَلَىٰ سَوَآءٍۢ ۖ وَإِنْ أَدْرِىٓ أَقَرِيبٌ أَم بَعِيدٌۭ مَّا تُوعَدُونَ
- 21:110 إِنَّهُۥ يَعْلَمُ ٱلْجَهْرَ مِنَ ٱلْقَوْلِ وَيَعْلَمُ مَا تَكْتُمُونَ
- 21:111 وَإِنْ أَدْرِى لَعَلَّهُۥ فِتْنَةٌۭ لَّكُمْ وَمَتَٰعٌ إِلَىٰ حِينٍۢ
- 21:112 قَٰلَ رَبِّ ٱحْكُم بِٱلْحَقِّ ۗ وَرَبُّنَا ٱلرَّحْمَٰنُ ٱلْمُسْتَعَانُ عَلَىٰ مَا تَصِفُونَ


===== _commentary/v16/work/s021/surah.r2/dictionary.md =====
# Dictionary: every branch of every focus root

Every root of the surah's words, each once, headed by the ayah and word where it first occurs; it also serves the later words listed with it.
One entry per branch: a Turkish label and Turkish glosses of its attested senses, then the classical dictionaries' own phrases with their source tags (ayn, sihah, tahdhib, maqayis, mufradat, jamhara). [kalıp] marks a sense the dictionaries attest only inside a fixed expression.
Identity roots come from the quran-data gateway. Word-scoped alternatives are cited analyses of this
exact word. **Echo roots** are observed but withheld mappings: sound-family candidates, not identity.

## ق ر ب (root_001212): 21:1 ٱقْتَرَبَ, 21:97 وَٱقْتَرَبَ, 21:109 أَقَرِيبٌ

- **B001** yakın olma, yaklaşma veya yaklaştırma — yakın olmak veya yaklaşmak · yaklaştırmak, yakına getirmek · yaklaşma · ses değişmesiyle yaklaşmak · suyu yakın kuyu · parçaları birbirine yakın, kısa yapılı
  أصل صحيح يدل على خلاف البعد (maqayis)؛ كرب الشيء دنا فليس من الباب وإنما هو من الإبدال من القرب (maqayis-ibdal)؛ قرب الشيء قربا ضد البعد (jamhara)؛ قرب الشيء يقرب قربا أي دنا والقرب ضد البعد (sihah)؛ القرب نقيض البعد والتقرب التدني إلى شيء والاقتراب الدنو والقرب البئر القريبة الماء والرجل القصير متقارب (tahdhib)؛ القرب والبعد يتقابلان ويستعمل ذلك في المكان (mufradat)
- **B002** zamanca yaklaşma veya yakın geçmişe ait olma — vaadin veya hesap vaktinin yaklaşması · son saatin yaklaşması · ürünün olgunlaşma vaktinin yaklaşması · güneşin batmaya yaklaşması · henüz taze olan tuzlu balık
  اقترب الوعد أي تقارب (sihah)؛ تقارب الزمان اقتراب الساعة وتقارب الزرع إذا دنا إدراكه والشيء إذا ولى وأدبر قد تقارب والقريب السمك المملح ما دام في طراءته (tahdhib)؛ في الزمان نحو اقترب للناس حسابهم (mufradat)؛ كربت الشمس دنت للمغيب (maqayis-ibdal)
- **B003** akrabalık ve yakın akraba — akrabalık, soy bağı · yakın akraba · yakın akrabalığı olan kimse
  فلان ذو قرابتي وهو من يقرب منك رحما والقربة والقربى القرابة (maqayis)؛ قريب الرجل مدانيه من نسب أم أو أب والجمع قرابة وقرباء وأقرباء (jamhara)؛ القرابة القربى في الرحم وهو قريبي وذو قرابتي وهم أقربائي وأقاربي (sihah)؛ القريب والقريبة ذو القرابة وفلان ذو قرابتي وذو مقربة وذو قربى (tahdhib)؛ في النسبة أولوا القربى والأقربون وذو قربى ولذي القربى والجار ذي القربى ويتيما ذا مقربة (mufradat)
- **B004** ayrıcalıklı yakın çevre — yakın kılınmış, gözde kişiler · hükümdarın özel çevresi, oturum arkadaşları ve yöneticileri · yakın kılınmış melekler

  خرز كتيم لا ينضح الماء (maqayis)؛ خرز كتيم لا يخرج منه الماء وسقاء كتيم (sihah)؛ كتمت المزادة تكتم كتوما إذا ذهب مرحها وسيلان الماء من مخارزها (tahdhib)
- **B005** siyah saç boyası karışımında kullanılan kırmızımsı bitki — siyah saç boyası karışımında kullanılan kırmızımsı boya bitkisi
  الكتم فنبات يختضب به (maqayis)؛ الكتم نبات يخلط مع الوسمة للخضاب الأسود (ayn)؛ الكتم شجر يخضب به الشعر (jamhara)؛ الكتم نبت يخلط بالوسمة يختضب به (sihah;tahdhib)؛ الكتم نبت فيه حمرة (tahdhib)
- **B006** atın dar burun deliği yüzünden nefesinin tutulması [kalıp] — atın dar burun deliği yüzünden nefesinin tutulması
  يقال للفرس إذا ضاق منخره عن نفسه قد كتم الربو

## ع و ن (root_001064): 21:112 ٱلْمُسْتَعَانُ

- **B002** yaşça orta evrede olan — yaşça orta evrede olan · ne genç ne yaşlı sığır · orta yaşlı veya evlenmiş kadın · orta yaşlı at · orta yaşta olanlar

# S021 Semantic Channel Discovery

## Parent Channels

### 1. P1 - Attention Becomes Answerability
- Semantic invariant: A message becomes morally operative through reception, inward retention, and accountable expression.
- Surface relation: direct; 21:1-3 moves from heedlessness and turning aside to listening, distracted hearts, and secret counsel, while 21:7 and 21:10 join revelation, reminder, knowledge, writing, and reason.
- Surprising reach: Hearing is reframed as an entire transmission system: the ear admits a signal, the heart either keeps or abandons it, and private speech eventually becomes a public claim.

#### Subchannel A. Distracted reception
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Sound reaches the ear, but distraction diverts the heart and bodily turning prevents reception from becoming understanding.
- Active motifs: auditory reception `quranic:root_000741:B001/m01`; attentive listening `quranic:root_000831:B006/m01`; lapse from vigilance `quranic:root_001097:B001/m01`; diversion by another concern `quranic:root_001382:B001/m01`; turning one's side away `quranic:root_001001:B005/m01`; heart as the seat of understanding `quranic:root_001248:B001/m01`; intellect restraining ignorance `quranic:root_001036:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 21:1 `غفلة، معرضون`; 21:2 `استمعوه`; 21:3 `لاهية قلوبهم`; 21:9 `نشاء`; 21:10 `تعقلون`
- Synthesis: The scene is not simple deafness. Sound crosses the outer threshold, but heedlessness, diversion, and a turned side interrupt its passage into the heart, making listening physically present yet cognitively uncompleted.

#### Subchannel B. Secret counsel becomes circulating speech
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Concealed thought is exchanged in a whisper, then leaves the private chamber as a report that can circulate among people.
- Active motifs: inward concealment `quranic:root_000697:B001/m01`; confidential exchange `quranic:root_001476:B005/m01`; unvoiced speech in the self `quranic:root_001272:B012/m01`; a saying spread among people `quranic:root_001272:B007/m01`; becoming a story on people's tongues `quranic:root_000299:B004/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 21:2 `ذكر محدث`; 21:3 `أسروا النجوى`; 21:4-5 `القول، قالوا`
- Synthesis: Privacy is a temporary container rather than a terminal state. The whispered judgment about the messenger passes from concealed interior speech into a repeatable public account, exposing how a communal narrative is manufactured from a private consultation.

#### Subchannel C. Inscription restores memory and judgment
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Revelation is received as a written, recall-producing object whose marks reactivate memory and restrain ignorance.
- Active motifs: written book or record `quranic:root_001283:B002/m02`; writing or engraving a message `quranic:root_001633:B003/m01`; recollection after absence `quranic:root_000516:B003/m01`; intellect that restrains ignorance `quranic:root_001036:B001/m01`; knowledge disclosed to the knower `quranic:root_001040:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 21:7 `نوحي، أهل الذكر، تعلمون`; 21:10 `أنزلنا إليكم كتابا فيه ذكركم، تعقلون`
- Synthesis: The book is both material inscription and cognitive instrument. Its ordered marks carry hidden instruction into durable form, call an absent truth back to mind, and let reason function as a restraint against heedless response.

### 2. P1 - Ruin Reduces Motion to Remnant
- Semantic invariant: Destruction proceeds by arresting movement, breaking organized settlement, and converting living form into cut or extinguished residue.
- Surface relation: direct; 21:6, 21:9, 21:11-13, and 21:15 trace destroyed settlements from approaching force through flight and forced return to harvested and extinguished remains.
- Surprising reach: The ruined community is simultaneously a shattered structure, a routed body, a reaped field, and a fire whose visible flame has fallen still.

#### Subchannel A. The settlement is broken as a structure
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Overwhelming force arrives, breaks the organized settlement, and eradicates its capacity to continue as a living whole.
- Active motifs: destructive breaking that crushes `quranic:root_001234:B002/m01`; falling into destruction and disappearance `quranic:root_001596:B001/m01`; eradication by cutting away `quranic:root_000321:B001/m01`; affliction arriving upon its object `quranic:root_000009:B011/m01`; overpowering severity `quranic:root_000079:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 21:5 `فليأتنا`; 21:6 `قرية أهلكناها`; 21:9 `أهلكنا المسرفين`; 21:11 `قصمنا من قرية`; 21:12 `أحسوا بأسنا`
- Synthesis: The village is treated as an integrated construction whose ruin begins with a crushing break. The force does not merely defeat inhabitants; it dismantles the settlement's continuity until no organized social body remains.

#### Subchannel B. Flight is driven back to its point of departure
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Feet strike the ground in rapid escape, but the route is reversed and the fugitives are ordered back toward the dwelling they abandoned.
- Active motifs: foot-strike against the ground `quranic:root_000593:B001/m01`; impelled flight `quranic:root_000593:B002/m01`; rapid departure `quranic:root_001476:B002/m01`; return to a prior direction or state `quranic:root_000544:B001/m01`; inhabited dwelling `quranic:root_000726:B002/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 21:9 `فأنجيناهم`; 21:12-13 `يركضون، لا تركضوا وارجعوا، مسكنكم`
- Synthesis: Escape and return form one reversed trajectory. The same bodies that accelerate away are redirected toward the material center of their privilege, turning the dwelling into the place where flight is arrested and accountability catches up.

#### Subchannel C. Harvested stalks and quenched flame
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A living collective is converted first into severed crop and then into a fire whose activity and vital motion have ceased.
- Active motifs: cutting ripe growth `quranic:root_000327:B001/m01`; stilling a flame while embers remain `quranic:root_000437:B001/m01`; cessation of life or awareness after movement `quranic:root_000437:B003/m01`; causing a thing to assume a new state `quranic:root_000248:B002/m01`; fire consuming its feed `quranic:root_000043:B005/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 21:8 `يأكلون`; 21:15 `جعلناهم حصيدا خامدين`
- Synthesis: The paired images separate two terminal operations: harvesting severs growth, while quenching removes active flame. Together they materialize ruin as a transformation from standing, consuming life into cut matter and silent residual heat.

### 3. P2 - The Cosmos Is Framed, Opened, and Stabilized
- Semantic invariant: Habitable order depends on constructed boundaries that are firmly joined, selectively opened, and anchored against destabilizing motion.
- Surface relation: direct; 21:16 rejects purposeless construction, while 21:30-32 presents joined heavens and earth, opened seams, stabilizing mountains, passes, and a protected roof.
- Surprising reach: Cosmology takes the form of architecture and civil engineering: seam-work, reservoirs, roof spans, anchors, and cut passages make life possible.

#### Subchannel A. A guarded overhead enclosure
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Earth occupies the lower plane beneath a raised, sheltering roof whose span is watched and preserved.
- Active motifs: high roof `quranic:root_000720:B001/m01`; sky as whatever rises and shades `quranic:root_000745:B004/m01`; raised canopy `quranic:root_001000:B002/m01`; earth as the lower counterpart of sky `quranic:root_000025:B001/m01`; active guarding and preservation `quranic:root_000342:B001/m01`; enclosing canopy or house `quranic:root_001315:B006/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 21:16, 21:19 `السماء والأرض`; 21:22 `العرش`; 21:30 `السماوات والأرض`; 21:32 `السماء سقفا محفوظا`
- Synthesis: The sky is not only elevated space but a roofed boundary over a lower floor. Guarding makes that span an actively maintained enclosure, so cosmic preservation resembles the upkeep of a shelter rather than inert distance.

#### Subchannel B. A sealed seam is opened for flow
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Joined edges are first fused, then separated along a seam whose opening permits expansion and flow.
- Active motifs: joining a split until it closes `quranic:root_000539:B001/m01`; opening what had been joined `quranic:root_001126:B001/m01`; separation of connected parts `quranic:root_000170:B001/m01`; widening an opening until something can flow `quranic:root_001559:B003/m01`; cloud or dawn splitting open `quranic:root_001126:B003/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 21:16 `ما بينهما`; 21:28 `ما بين أيديهم`; 21:30 `كانتا رتقا ففتقناهما`; 21:33 `النهار`
- Synthesis: Joining and opening are distinct operations in one mechanism. The former establishes an intact boundary; the latter creates a controlled aperture, reframing creation as the conversion of sealed continuity into productive passage.

#### Subchannel C. Anchors restrain sway and passes guide movement
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Fixed masses arrest lateral instability while broad openings through them channel travelers along intelligible routes.
- Active motifs: firm anchoring `quranic:root_000564:B001/m01`; swaying and lateral disturbance `quranic:root_001459:B001/m01`; broad mountain pass `quranic:root_001131:B001/m01`; extended traversable road `quranic:root_000672:B001/m01`; gentle guidance toward a path `quranic:root_001583:B001/m01`; protected straight route `quranic:root_000342:B007/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 21:31 `رواسي أن تميد بهم، فجاجا سبلا، يهتدون`; 21:32 `محفوظا`
- Synthesis: Stability and mobility are not opposites here. Mountains stop uncontrolled sway, while passes cut through the same resistant mass to produce directed movement, making guidance a property of engineered terrain.

### 4. P2 - Life and Luminaries Navigate Ordered Media
- Semantic invariant: Water, living bodies, and celestial bodies move through bounded media by channels, circuits, and buoyant motion.
- Surface relation: direct; 21:30 makes water the medium of life, and 21:33 places night, day, sun, and moon in swimming orbits.
- Surprising reach: A river, a ship, and a celestial orbit become homologous routing systems rather than separate natural domains.

#### Subchannel A. Water emerges, is conveyed, and vivifies
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Water becomes visible and abundant, is conveyed through channels, and changes dry matter into living growth.
- Active motifs: water as substance `quranic:root_001458:B001/m01`; water appearing or increasing `quranic:root_001458:B002/m01`; conveying water by pouring or irrigation `quranic:root_001458:B003/m01`; earth revived by rain and vegetation `quranic:root_000383:B002/m01`; living creature endowed with life `quranic:root_000383:B003/m01`; river cutting a flowing channel through earth `quranic:root_001559:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 21:20 `النهار`; 21:30 `من الماء كل شيء حي`; 21:33 `النهار`
- Synthesis: Water is not a static ingredient. Its appearance, conveyance, and channel-cutting describe a causal sequence in which motion through earth becomes the material condition for living form.

#### Subchannel B. Celestial motion resembles swimming and shipping
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Sun and moon traverse circular tracks as swimmers or vessels moving within a containing medium.
- Active motifs: swimming or swift running `quranic:root_000666:B004/m01`; circular motion `quranic:root_001177:B001/m01`; celestial track `quranic:root_001177:B002/m01`; ship circling through water `quranic:root_001177:B003/m01`; sun `quranic:root_000818:B001/m01`; moon and its light `quranic:root_001255:B001/m01`; night darkness `quranic:root_001392:B001/m01`; daylight opening `quranic:root_001559:B002/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 21:20 `الليل والنهار`; 21:22, 21:26 `يسبحون، سبحانه`; 21:33 `خلق الليل والنهار والشمس والقمر كل في فلك يسبحون`
- Synthesis: The orbit is rendered as a navigable channel rather than empty abstraction. Swimming, shipping, and circular tracking supply a common mechanics for bodies that remain distinct while moving through one ordered expanse.

### 5. P2 - Sovereignty Operates Through Disciplined Service
- Semantic invariant: Legitimate order flows from a single authority through tireless service, bounded speech, intercession, and eventual accountability.
- Surface relation: direct; 21:19-20 and 21:22-29 contrast unwearied servants who act by command with rival divine claims that must answer for themselves.
- Surprising reach: The passage activates a court and service household in which rank is shown less by display than by controlled speech, assigned work, and inability to evade questioning.

#### Subchannel A. Tireless service without slackening
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Subordinate agents persist in worship and work without exhaustion, interruption, or release from their assigned relation.
- Active motifs: obedient worship `quranic:root_000973:B003/m01`; praise as worship `quranic:root_000666:B001/m01`; slackening after intensity `quranic:root_001125:B001/m01`; strength cut off by exhaustion `quranic:root_000320:B003/m01`; intentional work `quranic:root_001046:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 21:19 `عبادته، لا يستحسرون`; 21:20 `يسبحون، لا يفترون`; 21:25-27 `فاعبدون، عباد، بأمره يعملون`
- Synthesis: Negated fatigue defines a continuous service process. Worship, praise, observance, and work are not interchangeable labels; they are distinct operations held together by unbroken assignment to one authority.

#### Subchannel B. Courtly precedence and intercession
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Honored servants do not speak ahead of authority; any intercessor joins another's case only within accepted limits.
- Active motifs: binding command `quranic:root_000051:B002/m01`; office and authority `quranic:root_000051:B003/m01`; sovereign hand or power `quranic:root_001693:B005/m01`; intercessor joining another's cause `quranic:root_000802:B002/m01`; acceptance rather than displeasure `quranic:root_000569:B001/m01`; solicitous fear `quranic:root_000803:B003/m01`; precedence in speech or action `quranic:root_000671:B001/m01`; authoritative speaker `quranic:root_001272:B004/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 21:27 `لا يسبقونه بالقول، بأمره`; 21:28 `بين أيديهم، يشفعون إلا لمن ارتضى، مشفقون`
- Synthesis: Intercession is not autonomous patronage. It is a constrained act inside a ranked court, where precedence, accepted standing, and fear-aware care define who may join a case and when speech can occur.

#### Subchannel C. Claims are returned as questions and recompense
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Alleged authorities face questioning, truth is established, and a wrongful claim returns to its claimant as recompense.
- Active motifs: question and demand `quranic:root_000661:B001/m01`; reciprocal questioning `quranic:root_000661:B004/m01`; establishing and displaying truth `quranic:root_000347:B005/m01`; imposing judgment on another `quranic:root_001272:B010/m01`; recompense matching an act `quranic:root_000244:B001/m01`; grievance seeking redress `quranic:root_000967:B003/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 21:23 `لا يسأل، وهم يسألون`; 21:24 `هاتوا برهانكم، الحق`; 21:29 `نجزيه جهنم، نجزي الظالمين`
- Synthesis: Questioning and recompense form a return circuit. A claim to independent authority cannot remain a free assertion; it is brought into proof, converted into a case, and answered by an outcome corresponding to the claim.

### 6. P3 - Mortal Life Is Tasted and Assayed
- Semantic invariant: Finitude is known through bodily experience, while alternating good and evil expose the material hidden inside a person.
- Surface relation: direct; 21:34-35 denies bodily permanence, makes every self taste death, and names good and evil as a test.
- Surprising reach: Testing joins the mouth and the furnace: death is tasted, circumstances are experienced, and character is assayed like material under heat.

#### Subchannel A. Finitude enters through taste
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A living self encounters mortality as an ingested experience that removes force and ends any claim to bodily permanence.
- Active motifs: tasting food or an experience `quranic:root_000526:B001/m01`; loss of life and force `quranic:root_001454:B001/m01`; enduring without rapid decay `quranic:root_000429:B001/m01`; the life-bearing self `quranic:root_001533:B011/m01`; embodied human `quranic:root_000120:B002/m01`; totality enclosing every member `quranic:root_001315:B003/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 21:34 `لبشر، الخلد، مت`; 21:35 `كل نفس ذائقة الموت`
- Synthesis: Mortality is neither distant information nor a class applied from outside. Taste makes it an intimate bodily event, while the contrast with permanence exposes the human body as a temporary bearer of force rather than an enduring container.

#### Subchannel B. Good and evil reveal composition
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Alternating conditions test a subject until an inward quality becomes visible, as material is assayed under trial.
- Active motifs: test that reveals a condition `quranic:root_000153:B002/m01`; assaying metal and human character `quranic:root_001128:B001/m01`; gaining knowledge by experiencing a thing `quranic:root_000526:B002/m01`; beneficial good `quranic:root_000452:B001/m01`; evil or injury `quranic:root_000787:B001/m01`; tribulation and ordeal `quranic:root_001128:B004/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 21:35 `نبلوكم بالشر والخير فتنة`
- Synthesis: Good and evil are two test media rather than final verdicts. Their opposed pressures expose what the subject is made of, giving moral trial the mechanics of an assay that reveals composition by reaction.

### 7. P3 - Sudden Assault Collapses Claimed Defenses
- Semantic invariant: An unannounced strike defeats bodily guards, external protectors, and the expectation of delay.
- Surface relation: direct; 21:38-43 depicts a promised event arriving suddenly, fire reaching faces and backs, failed repulsion, and protectors unable to protect themselves.
- Surprising reach: Eschatological surprise is rendered as a tactical breach in which shields, sentries, companions, and response time all fail together.

#### Subchannel A. Arrival outruns recognition
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A threatened event enters without preparation, stuns its targets, encloses them, and denies time for response.
- Active motifs: sudden surprise `quranic:root_000135:B001/m01`; stunned bewilderment `quranic:root_000157:B001/m01`; coming and arrival `quranic:root_000009:B001/m01`; affliction arriving `quranic:root_000009:B011/m01`; explicit threat `quranic:root_001662:B002/m01`; evil descending and enclosing `quranic:root_000381:B001/m01`; waiting or granting delay `quranic:root_001520:B002/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 21:38 `الوعد`; 21:40 `تأتيهم بغتة فتبهتهم، لا ينظرون`; 21:41 `حاق`
- Synthesis: Surprise is a sequence: arrival precedes recognition, bewilderment blocks action, enclosure removes an exit, and refused delay prevents recovery. The event succeeds by collapsing response time before defenses can be organized.

#### Subchannel B. Fire reaches both face and back
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A body exposed on both sides cannot use hand, barrier, or ally to repel advancing fire.
- Active motifs: burning fire `quranic:root_001564:B002/m01`; face and frontal aspect `quranic:root_001630:B001/m01`; back as the opposite side of the body `quranic:root_000970:B002/m01`; warding or withholding `quranic:root_001308:B002/m01`; driving something back `quranic:root_000555:B002/m01`; aid that makes one prevail `quranic:root_001510:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 21:39 `يكفون عن وجوههم النار ولا عن ظهورهم، ينصرون`; 21:40 `ردها`
- Synthesis: Face and back establish total bodily exposure. Repulsion and aid are separate failed operations: the victims cannot turn the threat aside themselves, and no external force arrives to compensate for that failure.

#### Subchannel C. Guardians cannot guard themselves
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Watchers, barriers, protective force, and safeguarding companionship are invoked as a defense system that cannot secure its own agents.

- Ayah anchors: 21:40 `لا ينظرون`; 21:42 `من يكلؤكم بالليل والنهار`; 21:43 `آلهة تمنعهم، نصر أنفسهم، يصحبون`
- Synthesis: This is a layered security scene rather than a single denial of help. Sentry, obstacle, protective strength, and close escort each name a different defensive function, yet the system fails because none possesses independent security.

### 8. P3 - Extension and Reduction Are Made Exact
- Semantic invariant: Time, territory, and moral weight are finite quantities whose apparent extension is countered by exact reduction and measurement.
- Surface relation: direct; 21:44 contrasts lengthened lifetime with earth diminished at its edges, and 21:47 installs just balances sensitive to a mustard seed.
- Surprising reach: Political contraction and final judgment share the logic of a measured boundary: no extension is indefinite and no reduction is too small to register.

#### Subchannel A. Long duration meets an eroding edge
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Enjoyment and lifespan extend, but territorial breadth is progressively removed from its outer boundary.
- Active motifs: loss of part from a whole `quranic:root_001542:B001/m01`; edge and terminal boundary `quranic:root_000931:B001/m01`; breadth and side `quranic:root_001001:B001/m01`; lifespan extended in time `quranic:root_001044:B001/m01`; prolonged duration `quranic:root_000959:B003/m01`; overpowering conquest `quranic:root_001098:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 21:42 `معرضون`; 21:44 `متعنا، طال عليهم العمر، نأتي الأرض ننقصها من أطرافها، الغالبون`
- Synthesis: Temporal extension creates an illusion of secure breadth, while edge-loss reveals the opposite process already underway. The scene measures power by what remains inside a shrinking boundary, not by how long possession has lasted.

#### Subchannel B. The balance registers a mustard seed
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A straight scale receives an exact weight, compares it without distortion, and accounts even for the smallest seed.
- Active motifs: estimating by weight `quranic:root_001645:B001/m01`; balance of justice `quranic:root_001645:B002/m01`; comparison by alignment `quranic:root_001645:B003/m01`; equitable judgment `quranic:root_001224:B001/m01`; straight balance `quranic:root_001224:B004/m01`; measurable weight `quranic:root_000202:B004/m01`; germinating seed `quranic:root_000286:B001/m01`; mustard seed `quranic:root_000401:B001/m01`; sufficiency in completing an account `quranic:root_001310:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 21:47 `نضع الموازين القسط، مثقال حبة من خردل، أتينا بها، كفى بنا حاسبين`
- Synthesis: The scene separates instrument, operation, standard, and test object. Straightness prevents distortion, comparison determines equivalence, and the mustard seed pressures the scale at its lower limit without escaping the account.

### 9. P4 - Discernment Moves from External Light to Inward Return
- Semantic invariant: Truth becomes discernible first as a separating light and then as an inward capacity to reverse inherited error.
- Surface relation: direct; 21:48, 21:50-51 introduce criterion, illumination, reminder, and right guidance, while 21:64-65 and 21:67 depict a return to the self followed by renewed inversion.
- Surprising reach: Illumination is both optical and judicial: it separates forms outside the observer and enables the observer to turn judgment back upon the self.

#### Subchannel A. Light marks a separating criterion
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A descended reminder emits light and functions as a marker that distinguishes one course from another.
- Active motifs: spread illumination `quranic:root_000919:B001/m01`; light and radiance `quranic:root_000920:B001/m01`; reminder that restores presence `quranic:root_000516:B009/m01`; distinction between two things `quranic:root_001148:B001/m01`; delivering something downward `quranic:root_001492:B002/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 21:48 `الفرقان وضياء وذكرا`; 21:50 `ذكر مبارك أنزلناه`
- Synthesis: Criterion and light are distinct but cooperating functions. Illumination makes a field visible; separation marks the meaningful difference within that field; reminder preserves the distinction after the first encounter.

#### Subchannel B. Reason returns judgment to the self
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A mind turns back from inherited misdirection, inspects itself, and briefly reaches disclosed knowledge.
- Active motifs: intellect restraining ignorance `quranic:root_001036:B001/m01`; return from an error or act `quranic:root_000544:B003/m01`; inward mind and apprehension `quranic:root_001533:B013/m01`; knowledge disclosed `quranic:root_001040:B001/m01`; deviation from a right course `quranic:root_000913:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 21:51 `رشده، عالمين`; 21:54 `في ضلال`; 21:64-65 `رجعوا إلى أنفسهم، علمت`; 21:67 `أفلا تعقلون`
- Synthesis: The decisive movement is reflexive: judgment that had been projected onto Abraham returns to the judges themselves. Reason acts as a restraint against inherited direction, though the subsequent reversal shows how fragile that inward disclosure remains.

### 10. P4 - Fabricated Power Is Tested and Reversed
- Semantic invariant: Made objects are subjected to breakage, speech, utility, and fire tests that expose their inability to exercise the power assigned to them.

- Surprising reach: The idol dispute resembles destructive testing in a workshop: form, articulation, function, and thermal resistance are examined one operation at a time.

#### Subchannel A. Shaped bodies become fragments
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Crafted images are treated as bodies, then cut and broken until only fragments and one larger specimen remain.

- Synthesis: The scene distinguishes fabrication from destruction. A modeled form acquires the social status of a body, but breaking returns it to disconnected material pieces, while the surviving large object becomes a controlled test specimen.

#### Subchannel B. A speechless object fails the utility test
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: The remaining object is asked to speak and is then tested for its capacity to provide benefit or inflict harm.

- Synthesis: Speech and utility are separate tests. The idol cannot supply testimony about the deed, then fails the more basic functional contrast between benefit and harm, leaving worship attached to an object that cannot participate in either operation.

#### Subchannel C. The punitive furnace becomes cool safety
- Reading type: mixed

### 16. P5 - Community Integrity Alternates with Cutting

- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Diverse members are gathered as one kind, one religious course, and one direction of worship.
- Active motifs: community or type `quranic:root_000053:B004/m01`; shared religion and way `quranic:root_000053:B005/m01`; union in one direction `quranic:root_001631:B005/m01`; divine unity without partner `quranic:root_001631:B004/m01`; things proceeding on one manner `quranic:root_001222:B006/m01`; worshipful obedience `quranic:root_000973:B003/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 21:74 `القرية`; 21:92 `هذه أمتكم أمة واحدة، أنا ربكم فاعبدون`
- Synthesis: Unity is both composition and orientation. Members belong to one collective kind because they share a course and face one object of worship, not merely because they occupy the same social container.

#### Subchannel B. A shared affair is cut into portions
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: An integral affair is divided, apportioned, and converted into separate groups despite the possibility of regathering.
- Active motifs: division and apportionment `quranic:root_001240:B008/m01`; separated piece or faction `quranic:root_001240:B002/m01`; separation of connected parts `quranic:root_000170:B001/m01`; gathering dispersed parts `quranic:root_000259:B001/m01`; whole without deficiency `quranic:root_000259:B009/m01`; affair or condition `quranic:root_000051:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 21:77 `القوم`; 21:93 `تقطعوا أمرهم بينهم، كل إلينا راجعون`
- Synthesis: Cutting changes one affair into possessed portions. The factions are not simply different opinions; the imagery gives each a severed share of what had been a whole, while return preserves a future relation among the dispersed pieces.

### 17. P6 - Inscription Establishes Entitlement and Succession
- Semantic invariant: Right action is made durable by inscription, and prior inscription transfers ordered possession to worthy successors.
- Surface relation: direct; 21:94 records faithful striving, while 21:105 cites an earlier writing in which righteous servants inherit the earth.
- Surprising reach: Moral memory functions like a legal archive: effort receives an entry, scripture preserves title, and inheritance transfers possession without a new bargain.

#### Subchannel A. Striving enters an enduring register
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Purposeful faithful work becomes a written entry whose corresponding right cannot be denied or concealed.
- Active motifs: intentional work `quranic:root_001046:B001/m01`; righteousness opposed to corruption `quranic:root_000876:B001/m01`; trusted assent `quranic:root_000054:B002/m01`; directed striving `quranic:root_000709:B001/m01`; labor and earned action `quranic:root_000709:B002/m01`; writing or copying a text `quranic:root_001283:B002/m01`; written book or record `quranic:root_001283:B002/m02`; entering a name in a register `quranic:root_001283:B004/m01`; concealing a benefit `quranic:root_001307:B004/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 21:94 `يعمل من الصالحات وهو مؤمن، لا كفران لسعيه، له كاتبون`
- Synthesis: Work, striving, inscription, and entitlement are distinct stages. Faith gives the act its trusted orientation; the register makes it durable; and the denial of concealment ensures that earned relation cannot be erased from the account.

#### Subchannel B. Scripture conveys title to the righteous
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A prior book preserves a transfer by which righteous servants receive the earth as inherited possession.
- Active motifs: inheritance from predecessor to successor `quranic:root_001639:B001/m01`; transfer of possession without a new contract `quranic:root_001639:B002/m01`; inherited knowledge or book `quranic:root_001639:B003/m01`; writing and scripture `quranic:root_000621:B003/m01`; preservation against forgetting `quranic:root_000516:B003/m02`; worshipful obedience `quranic:root_000973:B003/m01`; righteousness `quranic:root_000876:B001/m01`; fertile earth `quranic:root_000025:B002/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 21:105 `كتبنا في الزبور من بعد الذكر أن الأرض يرثها عبادي الصالحون`; 21:106 `لقوم عابدين`
- Synthesis: The book behaves as both archive and instrument of conveyance. It preserves the remembered terms of succession, while inheritance names a transfer whose legitimacy rests on the recipients' formed character rather than a fresh exchange.

### 18. P6 - Openings Sort Moving Multitudes toward Opposed Ends
- Semantic invariant: Once a boundary opens, movement accelerates and is sorted into radically different receiving environments.
- Surface relation: direct; 21:96 and 21:98-103 move from an opened barrier and descending multitudes to fireward entry, then contrast those kept distant and welcomed without terror.
- Surprising reach: The eschatological scene resembles hydrology and crowd routing: an aperture releases a surge, successive arrivals enter a basin, and another stream is diverted toward safety.

#### Subchannel A. An opened barrier releases a descending surge
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A closed boundary opens and a multitude slips out, rushing and flowing down from every raised contour.
- Active motifs: opening a closed entrance `quranic:root_001124:B001/m01`; water bursting from an aperture `quranic:root_001124:B005/m01`; elevation above the ground `quranic:root_000298:B001/m01`; stacked rising contours `quranic:root_000298:B004/m01`; rapid rushing `quranic:root_001499:B002/m01`; slipping free by separation `quranic:root_001499:B003/m01`; self-propelled flow `quranic:root_001499:B004/m01`; totality enclosing every route `quranic:root_001315:B003/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 21:96 `فتحت يأجوج ومأجوج، من كل حدب ينسلون`
- Synthesis: Opening, release, descent, and flow form one mechanism. The people are not merely numerous; their motion takes on the behavior of liquid escaping containment and following every available gradient.

#### Subchannel B. The fire receives fuel in successive entries
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Pebble-like fuel and its worshippers arrive at a fiery destination in repeated entries, where burning and exhalation replace hearing.
- Active motifs: fuel cast into fire `quranic:root_000325:B004/m01`; pebbles or gravel `quranic:root_000325:B001/m01`; arriving at a destination or watering place `quranic:root_001640:B001/m01`; successive entry `quranic:root_001640:B007/m01`; forceful exhalation or groan `quranic:root_000634:B002/m01`; auditory reception `quranic:root_000741:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 21:98 `حصب جهنم، لها واردون`; 21:99 `ما وردوها`; 21:100 `زفير، لا يسمعون`
- Synthesis: The scene distinguishes material, route, entry, and furnace state. What arrives as fuel enters in a stream, while exhalation dominates the soundscape and ordinary hearing ceases to function.

#### Subchannel C. The protected are diverted into welcome
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Those marked by good are held at a distance from the furnace, spared its great terror, and met within a field of fulfilled desire.
- Active motifs: active distancing `quranic:root_000131:B003/m01`; good opposed to ugliness `quranic:root_000323:B001/m01`; terror before danger `quranic:root_001152:B001/m01`; aid that relieves the terrified `quranic:root_001152:B005/m01`; two parties meeting face to face `quranic:root_001372:B004/m01`; desire inclining toward an object `quranic:root_000825:B001/m01`; precious object of competition `quranic:root_001533:B010/m01`; stable permanence `quranic:root_000429:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 21:101 `الحسنى، عنها مبعدون`; 21:102 `ما اشتهت أنفسهم خالدون`; 21:103 `لا يحزنهم الفزع الأكبر، تتلقاهم الملائكة`
- Synthesis: Protection occurs by routing, not by endurance inside the furnace. Distance removes exposure, aid answers terror, and face-to-face reception replaces involuntary entry with welcome into a stable field of desire.

### 19. P6 - Promise Is Announced across Hidden Distance
- Semantic invariant: The event's timing remains undisclosed, but proclamation, equality of notice, and knowledge of hidden response keep communication accountable.
- Surface relation: direct; 21:97, 21:103-105, and 21:107-110 combine approaching promise, uncertain near or far timing, equal warning, revelation of one God, and knowledge of open and concealed speech.
- Surprising reach: Uncertainty concerns distance, not communicative failure: the herald may not know the arrival interval while still placing every hearer on equal notice.

#### Subchannel A. The promise is near in force but unknown in distance
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A promised event approaches, yet its precise temporal distance and appointment remain outside the herald's knowledge.
- Active motifs: temporal approach `quranic:root_001212:B002/m01`; nearness `quranic:root_001212:B001/m01`; remoteness `quranic:root_000131:B001/m01`; promise opening expectation `quranic:root_001662:B001/m01`; threatening promise `quranic:root_001662:B002/m01`; appointed time or place `quranic:root_001662:B003/m01`; acquired knowledge `quranic:root_000473:B001/m01`; time or occasion `quranic:root_000382:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 21:97 `اقترب الوعد الحق`; 21:103 `توعدون`; 21:109 `أقريب أم بعيد ما توعدون`; 21:111 `فتنة لكم ومتاع إلى حين`
- Synthesis: Nearness and appointment are not collapsed. The event has approaching force, but its measured interval remains unknown, preserving urgency without turning uncertainty into denial of the promise.

#### Subchannel B. Notice places all hearers on equal footing
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A revealed proclamation is made openly and evenly, orienting every addressee toward one object of worship.
- Active motifs: public notification `quranic:root_000022:B003/m01`; equality between parties `quranic:root_000766:B001/m01`; just middle and even position `quranic:root_000766:B006/m01`; divine revelation `quranic:root_001633:B004/m01`; articulated speech `quranic:root_001272:B001/m01`; divine unity without partner `quranic:root_001631:B004/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 21:108 `يوحى إلي، إلهكم إله واحد`; 21:109 `آذنتكم على سواء`
- Synthesis: Equality here is procedural. The herald cannot equalize responses or timing, but he can make notice nonexclusive, placing all hearers at an even communicative starting point before one announced claim.

#### Subchannel C. Open speech and concealed response remain known
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Loud outward speech and inwardly withheld speech occupy opposite sides of one field of knowledge.
- Active motifs: public utterance and raised voice `quranic:root_000269:B001/m01`; visible disclosure `quranic:root_000269:B002/m01`; hiding and covering `quranic:root_001284:B001/m01`; sound held back `quranic:root_001284:B002/m01`; knowledge disclosed to the knower `quranic:root_001040:B001/m01`; speech retained in the self `quranic:root_001272:B012/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 21:110 `يعلم الجهر من القول، ويعلم ما تكتمون`
- Synthesis: Public and concealed speech are different communicative states, not different epistemic jurisdictions. Raised voice makes speech socially visible; concealment withholds it from others, but neither operation removes it from knowledge.

### 20. P6 - Return Is Barred Locally and Guaranteed Cosmically
- Semantic invariant: Return is not a uniform cycle: a destroyed settlement is denied restoration, while creation as a whole is promised rebeginning.
- Surface relation: direct; 21:95 bars a ruined settlement from return, and 21:104 folds the sky while promising creation's return after its beginning.
- Surprising reach: The same return mechanism is selectively closed and opened, distinguishing irreversible historical ruin from reversible cosmic form.

#### Subchannel A. A ruined settlement cannot re-enter its former state
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Prohibition closes the route by which a destroyed community might regain its prior social form.
- Active motifs: prohibition and prevention `quranic:root_000313:B001/m01`; settlement as gathered people and place `quranic:root_001222:B001/m01`; destruction and disappearance `quranic:root_001596:B001/m01`; return to a former direction or state `quranic:root_000544:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: 21:95 `حرام على قرية أهلكناها أنهم لا يرجعون`
- Synthesis: The closure concerns restoration, not mere movement. A settlement already dismantled cannot reconstitute the gathered form it possessed, so return is barred at the level of social ontology.

#### Subchannel B. Folded creation is begun again
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: The sky is folded like a document, and creation is returned by repeating the operation of beginning.
- Active motifs: beginning joined to return `quranic:root_000090:B002/m01`; return after departure and repetition after a start `quranic:root_001058:B001/m01`; final return and destination `quranic:root_001058:B002/m01`; originating creation `quranic:root_000434:B002/m01`; folding layer upon layer `quranic:root_000960:B001/m01`; record that gathers and fixes `quranic:root_000677:B004/m01`; binding commitment of a promise `quranic:root_001662:B001/m02`
- Ayah anchors: 21:104 `نطوي السماء كطي السجل للكتب، كما بدأنا أول خلق نعيده، وعدا علينا`
- Synthesis: Folding suspends the present spatial arrangement without exhausting the material of order. Beginning and return become repeatable operations, and the promise guarantees that cosmic form can be reissued after being compacted like a closed record.

## Standalone Subchannels

### S1. P1 - The messenger's body requires provision
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Visible human embodiment is identified by gathered bodily form, exposed skin, eating, tasting, and dependence on sustenance.
- Active motifs: human as visible-skinned creature `quranic:root_000120:B002/m01`; bodily surface `quranic:root_000120:B001/m01`; gathered body `quranic:root_000245:B001/m01`; taking food `quranic:root_000043:B001/m01`; tasting and eating `quranic:root_000934:B001/m01`; livelihood and provision `quranic:root_000934:B004/m01`

- Synthesis: Humanity is materialized through dependence rather than reduced to appearance. Skin makes the body visible, bodily form gathers it, and eating connects that form to a continuing economy of provision.

### S2. P1 - Affluence fixes inhabitants inside a vulnerable settlement
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A gathered settlement supplies dwelling, inhabitants, hospitality, and abundant livelihood, but luxury turns that stability into complacent attachment.
- Active motifs: expansive luxury `quranic:root_000179:B001/m01`; inhabited dwelling `quranic:root_000726:B002/m01`; household inhabitants `quranic:root_000726:B003/m01`; settlement as gathered people and place `quranic:root_001222:B001/m01`; food gathered for a guest `quranic:root_001222:B003/m01`; prosperous condition `quranic:root_000934:B004/m02`
- Ayah anchors: 21:6, 21:11 `قرية`; 21:8 `الطعام`; 21:13 `ما أترفتم فيه ومسكنكم`
- Synthesis: The scene distinguishes settlement from luxury. Dwelling and provision organize a stable social habitat; luxury converts that stability into an attachment whose apparent security is exposed when inhabitants are ordered back to it.

## Cross-Pericope Channels

These channels relate scenes at their canonical placements below; they do not relocate or duplicate the local findings.

### X1. Opening changes the fate of what enclosure held
- Pericopes: P2 (21:16-33), P5 (21:74-93), and P6 (21:94-112), with whole-surah standalone S17
- Bridge: Repeated scene signature plus contrast: enclosure -> aperture -> release, with the released content becoming life, rescued relation, or judgmental surge.
- Canonical placements: P2 / Parent 3 / Subchannel B; P5 / Parent 13; P6 / Parent 18 / Subchannel A; Whole-surah / S17
- Synthesis: Opening is morally non-neutral. Its effect depends on what is released, the receiving environment, and the authority governing access; the well scene materializes productive opening as access that must also be cleared and maintained.

### X2. Speed is classified by control and endpoint
- Pericopes: P1 (21:1-15), P2 (21:16-33), P3 (21:34-47), and P5 (21:74-93), with whole-surah standalone S20
- Bridge: Contrast across a repeated scene signature: mover or force + route + endpoint. Ordered orbit, wind, and horse motion oppose panic and runaway haste.
- Canonical placements: P1 / Parent 2 / Subchannel B; P2 / Parent 4 / Subchannel B; P3 / S10; P5 / Parent 14 / Subchannel D; Whole-surah / S20
- Synthesis: Velocity is not the invariant that assigns value; governance, route, and endpoint are. Flight and haste lose command of their paths, whereas orbit, wind, and trained speed become effective through direction.

### X3. Direction scales from terrain to community
- Pericopes: P2 (21:16-33), P4 (21:48-73), P5 (21:74-93), and P6 (21:94-112), with whole-surah standalone S19
- Bridge: Role progression: marked path -> guide -> aligned community -> equal notice -> embodied journey and offering.
- Canonical placements: P2 / Parent 3 / Subchannel C; P4 / Parent 12 / Subchannel C; P5 / Parent 16 / Subchannel A; P6 / Parent 19 / Subchannel B; Whole-surah / S19
- Synthesis: Direction develops from spatial passage into social and moral coordination. Terrain, leader, community, proclamation, and rite successively occupy the orienting role, so guidance culminates in practiced movement and relinquishment rather than abstract agreement.

### X4. Speech moves from hidden formation to permanent answerability
- Pericopes: P1 (21:1-15), P3 (21:34-47), P4 (21:48-73), and P6 (21:94-112)
- Bridge: Causal sequence plus role progression: inward or secret speech -> heard or blocked message -> public claim and testimony -> known and registered response.
- Canonical placements: P1 / Parent 1 / Subchannel B; P1 / Parent 1 / Subchannel C; P3 / S9; P4 / Parent 11; P6 / Parent 19 / Subchannel B; P6 / Parent 19 / Subchannel C; P6 / Parent 17 / Subchannel A
- Synthesis: Speech changes containers and institutional roles without escaping account. What begins as concealed formation can be blocked in reception or exposed in testimony, yet finally remains known and writable.

### X5. Reckoning replaces chance with measured inscription
- Pericopes: P1 (21:1-15), P3 (21:34-47), and P6 (21:94-112), with whole-surah standalone S21
- Bridge: Causal sequence plus contrast: approaching account -> exact weighing -> durable register, opposed by concealed lots and deceptive play.
- Canonical placements: P1 / S4; P3 / Parent 8 / Subchannel B; P6 / Parent 17 / Subchannel A; Whole-surah / S21
- Synthesis: Moral quantity passes through arrival, measurement, and inscription. The lot game is the precise reversal: it allocates outcomes through opacity, appetite, and manipulable uncertainty rather than exposed measure.

### X6. Generation becomes succession through formed relations
- Pericopes: P4 (21:48-73), P5 (21:74-93), and P6 (21:94-112), with whole-surah standalone S22
- Bridge: Causal sequence plus role progression: household generation -> embodied birth and repair -> guided office -> inherited possession.
- Canonical placements: P4 / Parent 12 / Subchannel B; P4 / Parent 12 / Subchannel C; P5 / Parent 15 / Subchannel A; P5 / Parent 15 / Subchannel B; P6 / Parent 17 / Subchannel B; Whole-surah / S22
- Synthesis: Continuity is neither biology nor property alone. Relation must be repaired and embodied, formed into responsible service, and only then conveyed as succession.

### X7. Fire's object and governor reverse its outcome
- Pericopes: P1 (21:1-15), P3 (21:34-47), P4 (21:48-73), and P6 (21:94-112), with whole-surah standalone S18
- Bridge: Repeated scene signature plus role reversal: heat or fire meets an assigned object, while the governing role determines extinguishment, exposure, protection, nourishment, or punishment.
- Canonical placements: P1 / Parent 2 / Subchannel C; P3 / Parent 7 / Subchannel B; P4 / Parent 10 / Subchannel C; P6 / Parent 18 / Subchannel B; Whole-surah / S18
- Synthesis: Fire is a medium rather than a fixed verdict. Its governor and assigned object determine whether heat prepares food, loses force, leaves a target exposed, or consumes it.

### X8. Cutting a whole does not determine whether it can return
- Pericopes: P1 (21:1-15), P4 (21:48-73), P5 (21:74-93), and P6 (21:94-112)
- Bridge: Repeated scene signature plus contrast: integrated whole -> severing or folding -> divergent outcome.
- Canonical placements: P1 / Parent 2 / Subchannel A; P1 / Parent 2 / Subchannel C; P4 / Parent 10 / Subchannel A; P5 / Parent 16 / Subchannel B; P6 / Parent 20 / Subchannel A; P6 / Parent 20 / Subchannel B
- Synthesis: Decomposition does not itself settle the result. Identity, authority, and promise distinguish residue, exposed fabrication, accountable division, and material gathered for reissue.

- Ayah anchors: 21:16 `خلقنا`; 21:30 `فتقناهما، كفروا`; 21:47 `القسط`; 21:73 `الصلاة`; 21:81 `الريح`
- Synthesis: The scene materializes the surah's movement from concealed quality to public effect. Crushing and oil-mixing do not invent the fragrance; they release it into perception, while application gives it a bearer from which it can spread.

### S35. Whole-surah - A marriage is contracted, endowed, conveyed, and housed
- Reading type: latent/lexical

- Synthesis: This materializes the surah's repaired generative relations as a social and legal formation rather than biology alone. Contract, dower, movement, and shelter establish obligations and a new household before that relation can carry succession.
